title: My Name Is Nobody
text:
On his way home from Troy, Odysseus and twelve of his men entered a huge cave full of cheeses and lambs. Its owner, the one eyed giant Polyphemus, came home with his flocks, rolled an enormous stone across the entrance, and ate two of the men for supper. Odysseus wanted to kill him as he slept, but realized that they could never move the stone themselves. They would die trapped inside.

So he made a plan. His men sharpened a long stake of olive wood and hardened its point in the fire. Odysseus offered the giant strong wine he had brought, and Polyphemus drank bowl after bowl. He asked the stranger's name. Odysseus told him it was Nobody. The giant promised, as a favor, to eat Nobody last, and fell into a drunken sleep. The men heated the stake and drove it into his eye.

Polyphemus roared for help, and the other Cyclopes came to the cave and asked who was hurting him. Nobody is killing me, he cried. Then nothing is wrong, they said, and went away. In the morning the men escaped by clinging under the bellies of his sheep as he let them out to graze.

But once safely on the ship, Odysseus could not resist shouting back his real name. The blinded giant prayed to his father, Poseidon, and the rest of Odysseus's journey home became years of disaster.
lesson: Plan around the obstacle you cannot move, not just the enemy in front of you. And once you have won, resist the urge to boast; it can hand your enemy the means to strike back.
